title: GATE CS Topic Test — General Aptitude (Set 1)
titleEn: GATE CS Topic Test — General Aptitude (Set 1)

questions.questionTextEn: Scarcely _______ the server restarted when another memory leak triggered an alert.
questions.explanationEn: The correlative conjunction 'Scarcely ... when' requires subject-auxiliary inversion in the past perfect tense: 'Scarcely had the server restarted when...'.

questions.questionTextEn: Find the next number in the sequence: 3, 7, 15, 31, 63, ___.
questions.explanationEn: Each term follows a_{n+1} = 2*a_n + 1 (or 2^(n+1) - 1). Next term = 2*63 + 1 = 127.

questions.questionTextEn: In the sentence 'The sudden resignation of the CFO threw a spanner in the works of the merger', the idiom 'threw a spanner in the works' means:
questions.explanationEn: 'Throw a spanner in the works' is a standard English idiom meaning to disrupt or prevent a plan or process from succeeding.

questions.questionTextEn: Point P(3, 4) in the Cartesian plane is rotated 90° counterclockwise about the origin. What are its new coordinates?
questions.explanationEn: A 90° counterclockwise rotation about the origin maps (x, y) to (-y, x). Thus (3, 4) maps to (-4, 3).

questions.questionTextEn: Statements: (1) No mammal is a reptile. (2) All whales are mammals. Which conclusion necessarily follows?
questions.explanationEn: Since all whales belong to the set of mammals, and the set of mammals is disjoint from reptiles, no whale can be a reptile.

questions.questionTextEn: At what annual simple interest rate will a principal double itself in 8 years?
questions.explanationEn: For the principal P to double, interest I = P. Using I = P*R*T/100 => P = P*R*8/100 => R = 100/8 = 12.5%.

questions.questionTextEn: The committee's report was so _______ that even experts struggled to identify its primary recommendation.
questions.explanationEn: 'Convoluted' means extremely complex and difficult to follow, which fits why even experts struggled to find the main recommendation. 'Lucid', 'succinct', and 'transparent' all imply clarity.

questions.questionTextEn: A standard die has opposite faces summing to 7. If 1 is on top and 2 is facing South, and the die is rolled once toward the North (90° rotation), which number is now on top?
questions.explanationEn: When the die rolls North, the face previously facing South (2) rotates up to become the top face.

questions.questionTextEn: Two fair coins are tossed simultaneously. What is the probability of getting at least one tail?
questions.explanationEn: Sample space = {HH, HT, TH, TT}. Three outcomes have at least one tail (HT, TH, TT). Probability = 3/4.

questions.questionTextEn: In how many ways can a committee of 3 members be selected from 6 men and 4 women if at least 2 women must be on the committee?
A car leaves City A at 8:00 AM at 60 km/h. Another car leaves City A at 9:30 AM along the same highway at 80 km/h. At what time will the second car overtake the first?
questions.explanationEn: Head start of first car = 1.5 hr * 60 km/h = 90 km. Relative speed = 80 - 60 = 20 km/h. Catch-up time = 90 / 20 = 4.5 hours after 9:30 AM = 2:00 PM.

questions.questionTextEn: City planners added dedicated bus lanes along Main Avenue to reduce traffic congestion. Three months later, average car commute times on Main Avenue increased by 10%, so critics declared the policy a failure. Which of the following, if true, MOST seriously challenges the critics' claim?
optionsEn: Fuel prices dropped slightly during those three months.
The bus lanes were painted bright red for visibility.
Some drivers chose to avoid Main Avenue entirely.
Total passenger throughput on Main Avenue rose by 35% as thousands of commuters switched to faster buses.
questions.explanationEn: If total passenger throughput rose by 35% via faster buses, the policy succeeded in moving far more people efficiently even if solo car times rose, challenging the claim that it failed.

questions.questionTextEn: In a conference, all AI researchers are programmers, no programmer is a lawyer, and some managers are lawyers. Which statement CANNOT be true?
optionsEn: No manager is an AI researcher.
questions.explanationEn: Since all AI researchers are programmers and no programmer is a lawyer, the set of AI researchers and the set of lawyers are completely disjoint. Thus 'Some AI researchers are lawyers' is impossible.

questions.questionTextEn: The difference between compound interest (compounded annually) and simple interest on a sum of money at 10% per annum for 2 years is ₹120. What is the principal amount?
A can complete a task in 15 days and B in 20 days. They work together for 4 days, after which A leaves. How many more days will B take to finish the remaining work?

Two alloys A and B contain copper and zinc in the ratios 4 : 1 and 1 : 3 respectively. In what ratio should alloys A and B be mixed to obtain a new alloy containing copper and zinc in the ratio 1 : 1?
questions.explanationEn: Copper fractions: A has 4/5, B has 1/4, target is 1/2. By alligation: (1/2 - 1/4) : (4/5 - 1/2) = (1/4) : (3/10) = 5 : 6.

questions.questionTextEn: How many distinct permutations of the letters of the word 'STATISTICS' exist?
questions.explanationEn: 'STATISTICS' has 10 letters: S(3), T(3), I(2), A(1), C(1). Number of distinct permutations = 10! / (3! * 3! * 2!) = 3,628,800 / (6 * 6 * 2) = 3,628,800 / 72 = 50,400.

questions.questionTextEn: In a software firm, the ratio of male to female engineers is 3 : 2. If 40% of male engineers and 60% of female engineers work remotely, what percentage of all engineers work remotely?
questions.explanationEn: Assume 300 male and 200 female engineers (total 500). Remote engineers = 0.40*300 + 0.60*200 = 120 + 120 = 240. Percentage = (240/500)*100% = 48%.

questions.questionTextEn: In a 1000 m race, A beats B by 100 m and B beats C by 100 m. By how many meters does A beat C in the same 1000 m race (assuming constant speeds)?
questions.explanationEn: When A runs 1000 m, B runs 900 m. Ratio v_B/v_A = 0.9. Similarly v_C/v_B = 0.9, so v_C/v_A = 0.81. When A finishes 1000 m, C has run 810 m, so A beats C by 190 m.

questions.questionTextEn: In how many ways can 5 boys and 4 girls be seated in a row so that no two girls sit adjacent to each other?
questions.explanationEn: First arrange the 5 boys in 5! ways. This creates 6 gaps (before, between, and after the boys). Choosing and arranging 4 girls in these 6 gaps can be done in P(6, 4) = 6*5*4*3 ways. Total = 5! * P(6, 4).
